clue.text: No uniform well turned round should have tight fit

indicators.note: turned round tells us to read the interjection for well from right to left

parts.note: um is a hesitant interjection, like well

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so the following word staggers into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice that a well-made garment, turned about, ought to fit snugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned round' reverses the interjection; 'tight', meaning drunk, signals the anagram; 'should have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mufti is civilian dress worn by someone who normally wears a service uniform.

clue.text: Distance I can't get wrong, then copy store of data

parts.note: M is short for mile, a distance

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters go into a different order

parts.note: to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: Someone frustrated at a distance they cannot cover, then reduced to copying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ICANTGET as AGNETICT; 'then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic tape is a recording medium on which data was stored, notably for early computers.

clue.text: Old Bill's residence shut before predator turns up

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the whole run is read from the bottom

parts.note: a door pulled to is shut
pre is a prefix meaning before
a wolf is a predator

explanation.surface: The police station is shut before a predator arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' suggests the police, but here is Bill of Bill and Ben, the Flowerpot Men of 1950s British children's TV, who lived in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill of the British children's show lived in a large clay plant pot in a garden.

clue.text: Little picture for the fashionistas?

definitions.meaning: a small image set within a larger picture or page
read as two words, belonging to the fashionable in-crowd

explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small illustration inside a larger one; split, it means suited to the trendy crowd.

clue.text: Function to take position, giving approximate range

parts.note: a ball is a grand social function or dance
to park is to put oneself or a vehicle in position

explanation.surface: A social event where one takes a seat, giving a rough range.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpark figure or being in the ballpark means being within a rough, approximate range.

clue.text: Seat up, so it moves forward

parts.note: bum is British slang for the bottom one sits on

indicators.note: moves signals that the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone shifts in their seat and pushes forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges UPSOIT as PTIOUS; 'forward' is the adjective meaning pushy, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in the sense of presumptuous or pushy matches being self-assertive and conceited.

clue.text: Bricks I placed under base of wall

indicators.note: placed under puts the self after the wall letter in this down clue
base of a word written downward is its last letter

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: Someone puts a brick under the bottom of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is a brand of plastic interlocking toy bricks.

clue.text: One note held by Italian favourite taking to violinist's instruction

indicators.note: held by means the letters sit inside the dish

parts.note: pizza is a favourite Italian dish
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is a musical note
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single note held by a favourite Italian tune becomes an instruction to a fiddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link adding TO after PIZZICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Pizzicato is a musical direction telling string players to pluck rather than bow.

clue.text: Attached to an organ, right way up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: Something attached to a church organ, set the right way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests a musical instrument, but it is a body organ, the kidney.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the adjective relating to the kidneys, which are bodily organs.

clue.text: Decrease in exercises with Zulu protected by further drug, which could be OK!

indicators.note: in tells us the decrease is placed inside the word for exercises

parts.note: gym is physical exercise, as in a school gym lesson
a loss is a decrease

indicators.note: protected by means the letter is enclosed within the word for further

parts.note: again means further or in addition
Z is Zulu in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A slimmer's regime of exercise and drugs, with an approving OK at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: OK! is a British celebrity magazine, so the exclamation-marked definition names an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: OK! is a celebrity weekly printed on shiny paper, an example of this kind of publication.

clue.text: Obliging nature accompanies first of lawyers, dubiously

indicators.note: dubiously suggests the letters are arranged in a questionable new way
first of picks the opening letter of lawyers

explanation.surface: A good-natured person tags along with the head of a legal firm, of doubtful motive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubiously' shuffles ACCOMPANIES plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaisance is a willingness to please others or comply, an obliging disposition.

clue.text: PM accompanies man selling sugar, without teeth

parts.note: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister in the 1950s
Henry Tate founded the sugar firm Tate & Lyle

explanation.surface: A prime minister goes about with a sugar salesman who has lost his teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate & Lyle is a well-known British sugar refiner, founded partly by Henry Tate.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentate is a zoological adjective for animals lacking teeth, such as anteaters.

clue.text: Gondolier's familiar sight as upright character, singer on river

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the singer and character after the river letter

parts.note: the letter I is a single upright stroke
an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice

explanation.surface: A Venetian boatman's view described through a character and a singer on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto bridge spans the Grand Canal in Venice, a sight gondoliers pass constantly.

clue.text: I go from disease and you get us past old rash

indicators.note: past places the pronoun after the letter for old
I go from disease asks for those letters to leave the name of the illness

parts.note: impetigo is a contagious skin infection
the words I and go supply the letters to be removed
U is text-speak for you
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's instructions for recovering from a skin complaint, ending with a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like the skin complaint of the surface but is the adjective meaning hasty; 'past' puts US after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetuous and rash both describe acting hastily without forethought.

clue.text: Can's rising oxygen produced cross — something potentially explosive?

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the pair is read upward

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
to breed is to produce, so bred means produced
X is a cross

explanation.surface: Gas from a canister rises and makes someone cross, a dangerous situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns OBRED into DERBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinderbox is figuratively a volatile situation liable to flare up into violence.

clue.text: Cutting into arch, so nothing wasted

indicators.note: into means the cutting is placed inside the word for arch

parts.note: arch as an adjective means knowing or sly
a paring is a thin piece cut away

explanation.surface: Someone cutting into an architectural arch carefully, wasting nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arch' looks like the architectural noun but is the adjective meaning knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: To use something sparingly is to use it economically so that little is wasted.

clue.text: Horse around a vessel, eating last of millet

indicators.note: eating means the vessel takes the letter inside itself

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of millet

explanation.surface: A horse circles a container of millet feed and eats from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' looks like the animal, which the millet supports, but horse around is a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up and to horse around both mean to misbehave playfully.

clue.text: Doctor treats hip, he treats the mind

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A doctor deals with a hip, while another specialist deals with the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb, rearranging TREATSHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychotherapist, often shortened, is someone who treats mental and emotional problems.

clue.text: 22 getting close, overheard

indicators.note: overheard tells us to take the sound of the phrase rather than its spelling

parts.note: to tighten is to make or get closer together

explanation.surface: Something huge is approaching, and someone has caught it by ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 refers to the answer of 22-down, GIANT; TIGHTEN said aloud resembles the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person or thing of enormous size or power, a synonym for a giant.

clue.text: Interception of rocket by Paul, say, a drama

indicators.note: interception of the rocket means it is broken into by the papal figure

parts.note: to rocket is to rise sharply, to soar
Paul is the name of several popes, so a pope is an example

explanation.surface: A missile is intercepted by someone called Paul, which makes a dramatic story.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is also the setter's name, a neat touch; 'by' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a serial drama on television or radio.

clue.text: Might noses be chosen?

parts.note: noses are notoriously ..., so the clue asks for the word meaning selected, read in that nose-picking sense

explanation.definitionFit: Chosen is a synonym of this word, and noses are also said to be this when fingers are put to work.

clue.text: Well I'm blowed! Bald, shaved and pink!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like well I'm blowed

indicators.note: shaved means the word loses its outer edges

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at someone bald, shaven and pink-skinned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaved' trims BALD to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a pinkish-orange colour named after the sea organism.

clue.text: Sticks alongside pole, breaking like mad things

indicators.note: alongside places the sticks next to the rest
breaking means the pole letter cuts into the word for like

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
N is the north pole
bats are sticks used to strike a ball, as in cricket

explanation.surface: Sticks lying by a pole get broken, behaving like crazy things.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingbats is informal slang for silly or crazy people.

clue.text: Very great soldiers

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
soldier ants are a caste of ant

explanation.surface: Some very great soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: One word supplies two kinds of soldier: an American GI and a soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant as an adjective means of very great size.

clue.text: Member sees mount, but not top

indicators.note: not top means the first letter of the word is removed in this down clue

parts.note: to mount is to climb

explanation.surface: A club member sees a mountain but not its summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a member of the body, such as an arm or leg.

clue.text: 22, not the Messiah, claiming God holding book group back

indicators.note: claiming means the name takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: in Monty Python's Life of Brian, Brian is famously said to be not the Messiah

indicators.note: holding means the god's name contains the book letter

parts.note: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology

indicators.note: back means the word for group is read in reverse

parts.note: a gang is a group of people

explanation.surface: A huge figure, not the Messiah, claims a god holding a book and a group behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 points to 22-down, the word for a huge person. 'back' reverses the group word, 'holding' puts the book inside the god, and 'claiming' wraps both in the Python name.
explanation.definitionFit: Brobdingnag is the land of giants in Gulliver's Travels, so its adjective means gigantic.

clue.text: Former lover gatecrashing party in smart clothes with an accommodating manner

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here, so the smart word wraps round the rest

parts.note: fly is slang for sharp or smart

indicators.note: gatecrashing means the former lover gets inside the party

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An ex crashes a party where everyone is in smart clothes, behaving accommodatingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun (smart clothes) but is a verb, so FLY wraps LEXIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting flexibly means being adaptable and willing to accommodate others.

clue.text: Piece bearing letter about time for name

indicators.note: about means the piece goes round the time letter

parts.note: a Scrabble tile is a playing piece with a letter on it

explanation.surface: A game piece carrying a letter, with a time-related twist, stands for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name of a book, film or other work.
